name: HDMI Connector
short_description: A 19-pin high-definition multimedia interface connector used for transmitting uncompressed digital video and audio.
common_uses: HDTV inputs, computer monitor connections, single-board computer outputs (Raspberry Pi).
definition: An HDMI (High-Definition Multimedia Interface) connector is a 19-pin high-density compact digital connector. It is the universal standard for transmitting uncompressed digital video, multi-channel audio, and control data between multimedia devices.
working_principle: It routes digital video and audio over three Transition-Minimized Differential Signaling (TMDS) data channels and one clock channel. It includes DDC lines (I2C protocol) for device handshake and a 5V power line to read EDID data from turned-off screens.
types: HDMI Type-A (Standard), Mini-HDMI Type-C, and Micro-HDMI Type-D (used in compact cameras and Raspberry Pi 4).
construction: Houses 19 gold-plated pins on a thin plastic tongue inside a shielded metal D-shell connector housing.
electrical_characteristics: Low contact resistance, matched 100Ω differential impedance high-speed lines, and high EMI shield integrity.
symbol_description: Detailed 19-pin block displaying TMDS channels, DDC lines, hot-plug detect, and 5V power terminals.
formulas: TMDS differential pair impedance: Z_diff = 100 Ω.
applications: Television displays, gaming consoles, desktop computer graphics cards, and media projectors.
advantages: Carries uncompressed high-definition video and multi-channel audio in a single cable, standardized globally, supports copy protection (HDCP).
disadvantages: Extremely fine pin spacing is difficult to solder by hand, cables have length limits (typically under 10 meters without active boosters).
example_circuit_operation: An HDMI port is soldered to an MCU board. The high-speed TMDS lines are routed with exact length-matching as 100Ω differential pairs to the graphics controller, with TVS diodes added for ESD protection.
practical_tips: When routing high-speed HDMI TMDS differential traces on a PCB, ensure the traces have no vias and maintain a continuous ground reference plane directly beneath them to prevent signal skew and electromagnetic radiation.

interview_questions.question: How many pins does a standard Type-A HDMI connector have?
What is TMDS and how is it used in HDMI?
interview_questions.answer: Transition-Minimized Differential Signaling. It is a signaling standard that reduces copper electromagnetic radiation and uses differential pairs to transmit high-speed digital video data.

interview_questions.question: What is the purpose of the 5V pin (Pin 18) on the HDMI connector?
interview_questions.answer: It provides 5V power from the source to the sink device (display), allowing the source to read the display's EDID configuration data even when the display is powered off.

interview_questions.question: What is the function of the Hot Plug Detect (HPD) pin?
interview_questions.answer: It allows the source device to detect when an HDMI cable has been connected or disconnected, triggering the initialization handshake.

interview_questions.question: Why is differential trace length matching critical on HDMI PCBs?
interview_questions.answer: If the two traces in a differential pair are not length-matched, the signal arrival time differs (skew), causing phase errors and jitter that corrupt high-resolution video data.

references: HDMI Specification Document Version 1.4/2.0; high-speed board layout app notes.
